answer: Each identity files one lagoon sediment core in the canyon archive and locks a 70-credit bond. The core carries pigment layers from its lagoon plot, sealed to its key, with layer order logged. An auditor re-reads the core against the lagoon source record; a mismatch or reused core burns the bond. Filing costs 30 credits first, 30+5(k-1) for the k-th, and 5025 for the 1000th, so 1000 fakes pay 2,527,500 and lock 70,000. A rented-core ring fails because a borrowed core carries another plot's pigment sequence. An honest filer pays 30 once and recovers the bond after audit.
